entry.description: werner null-polynomial conjecture counterexample. the paper gives an explicit finite ring whose null polynomials are not closed under right multiplication and hence do not form a two-sided ideal, also yielding a torsion-free integer-algebra counterexample to a related 2014 problem. gpt-5.6 sol generated the counterexample and initial proof; the author independently verified the construction and simplified the proof.

entry.description: Parity of the partition function in quadratic progressions. The current primary source reports: For every square-free 1<D≡23 (mod 24), the values p((Dm^2+1)/24) with (m,6)=1 contain infinitely many of each parity; moreover m_odd≤12h(-D)+2 and m_even≤(12h(-D)+2) product over primes l dividing D of (l+1). The v4 source additionally reports: Corollary 2, due to Qi-Yang Zheng: liminf as X tends to infinity of N_odd(X)/sqrt(X) is at least 243/(64 sqrt(6) pi^5), hence the number of n<=X for which p(n) is odd is >> sqrt(X), improving the preceding lower bound by a log log X factor.
